candidates.name: WILD-PATHNAME-P
candidates.law: Check for wildcard components in a pathname globally or in one designated component.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A wildcard name causes the name-specific test to be true; a concrete type-only field remains false.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: A wildcard in the name causes the type-only test to be true.

candidates.name: CONCATENATED-STREAM-STREAMS
candidates.law: Return the remaining associated input streams of a concatenated stream.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Construct from I,J and inspect the associated sequence before reads.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Return an output stream not associated with the concatenation.

candidates.name: TRANSLATE-LOGICAL-PATHNAME
candidates.law: Apply ordered logical-host translation rules to a logical pathname until a physical pathname results.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Matching translation of a logical host to a physical host produces the mapped physical pathname.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Silently succeed when no translation rule matches; host-defined lookup is not assumed universal.

candidates.name: TRANSLATE-PATHNAME
candidates.law: Translate an explicit source pathname matching FROM-WILDCARD into TO-WILDCARD with corresponding wildcard substitutions.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: An explicit wildcard source name captured by FROM appears in the substituted TO name.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Treat a non-matching source as an ordinary matched pathname.

candidates.name: STREAM-ERROR-STREAM
candidates.law: Return the offending stream recorded in a stream-error condition.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A stream-error condition generated for stream S exposes S via STREAM-ERROR-STREAM.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Return an unrelated stream not referenced by the condition.

candidates.name: EXPORT
candidates.law: Mark an accessible symbol external in its target package.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: FIND-SYMBOL reports :EXTERNAL for an exported symbol.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Exporting a symbol silently changes its identity.

candidates.name: FIND-SYMBOL
candidates.law: Look up a symbol by exact name and return both its identity and :INTERNAL, :EXTERNAL, :INHERITED or absence.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: After INTERN of 'X' in P, FIND-SYMBOL of X in P reports an accessible symbol and status.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Return a symbol from an unrelated package with the wrong status.

candidates.name: FIND-PACKAGE
candidates.law: Resolve a registered package by its primary name, nickname, or package designator.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A registered package nickname resolves to the same package object.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Invent a new package if the name is not registered.

candidates.name: FIND-ALL-SYMBOLS
candidates.law: Collect interned symbols whose names exactly equal the requested string across known packages.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: An interned X is returned among same-named symbols; a different name is excluded.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Include a symbol whose name does not match.

candidates.name: IMPORT
candidates.law: Make an existing symbol present in a target package without changing symbol identity.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Import S into P; FIND-SYMBOL returns that very S.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Silently replace a conflicting distinct symbol of the same name.

candidates.name: LIST-ALL-PACKAGES
candidates.law: Return the set/list of currently registered package objects.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: After MAKE-PACKAGE of fresh P, the resulting P appears in the registry.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Include a package that has never been registered.

candidates.name: RENAME-PACKAGE
candidates.law: Change a package's name/nicknames while preserving the package identity.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A fresh nickname resolves to the renamed package object.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Rename creates an unrelated package and loses existing symbols.

candidates.name: SHADOW
candidates.law: Establish a local symbol of a specified name as a shadowing identity, preventing same-name inherited ambiguity.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A shadowing name remains locally accessible despite used package exports.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: An inherited conflicting symbol overrides the shadowing symbol.

candidates.name: SHADOWING-IMPORT
candidates.law: Import the specified symbol as a shadowing symbol, using its exact identity.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A target package resolves the given imported S rather than a conflicting inherited symbol.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Create a fresh unrelated symbol instead of importing S.

candidates.name: DELETE-PACKAGE
candidates.law: Delete a registered package from the package registry according to the defined package lifecycle.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: FIND-PACKAGE no longer resolves a successfully deleted package by its former registered name.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Delete an unrelated package while leaving the requested one registered.

candidates.name: MAKE-PACKAGE
candidates.law: Create a new package registered under a distinct given name with specified initial use relations.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A fresh name resolves to the created package after the call.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Create a second conflicting package under an already registered name without error.

candidates.name: UNEXPORT
candidates.law: Change an accessible external symbol in a package to internal status without removing its identity.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Previously external S is still present but reports :INTERNAL after UNEXPORT.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: UNEXPORT silently removes S from the package.

candidates.name: UNINTERN
candidates.law: Remove a symbol from its package's present-symbol set, respecting shadowing and inherited-name behavior.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: UNINTERN of sole local S removes that local presence.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Remove unrelated symbols or pretend the symbol still belongs to the same present-symbol set.

candidates.name: UNUSE-PACKAGE
candidates.law: Remove one use/inheritance relation without erasing symbols physically present in the target package.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: After UNUSE-PACKAGE, unrelated locally present symbols remain accessible.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Remove all local symbols when removing only one used package.

candidates.name: USE-PACKAGE
candidates.law: Add a package use relation, making its external symbols accessible subject to name-conflict checking.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: The external X of used P becomes inherited in an otherwise conflict-free target.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Silently resolve two conflicting inherited identities as though they were the same symbol.

candidates.name: PACKAGE-NAME
candidates.law: Return a package's primary registered name.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: After MAKE-PACKAGE with primary name P, PACKAGE-NAME identifies P.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Return a nickname instead of the primary name.

candidates.name: PACKAGE-NICKNAMES
candidates.law: Return the alternative names registered for a package.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: The nicknames supplied at creation appear in PACKAGE-NICKNAMES.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Replace the primary name with a nickname in the primary-name field.

candidates.name: PACKAGE-SHADOWING-SYMBOLS
candidates.law: Return the symbols explicitly recorded as shadowing in one package.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: After SHADOW of X, the package shadowing set contains that local X.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Return an unrelated imported symbol as a shadowing member.

candidates.name: PACKAGE-USE-LIST
candidates.law: Return the packages whose external symbols a target package uses.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: USE-PACKAGE of P into Q makes P appear in Q's use-list.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Return a package that Q does not use.

candidates.name: PACKAGE-USED-BY-LIST
candidates.law: Return the reverse relation: packages that use this package.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: After Q uses P, Q appears in PACKAGE-USED-BY-LIST of P.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Confuse used-by with P's own use-list.

candidates.name: PACKAGEP
candidates.law: Recognize package objects as distinct from package names/string designators.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: MAKE-PACKAGE result is PACKAGEP true; string containing its name is not a package object.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Treat any package-name string as an actual package object.

candidates.name: PACKAGE-ERROR-PACKAGE
candidates.law: Extract the package referent recorded in a package-error condition.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A package-error condition tied to package P exposes its recorded package referent.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Return a different unrelated package as the error referent.

candidates.name: COPY-READTABLE
candidates.law: Copy a readtable's character syntax and macro associations into a separately mutable target/readtable.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Mutating a copied readtable does not mutate the source table's mapping.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: A copy shares writable syntax associations with the original.

candidates.name: READTABLEP
candidates.law: Recognize an actual readtable object, not any string or arbitrary datum.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: COPY-READTABLE produces an object for which READTABLEP is true.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Return true for an ordinary character or integer.

candidates.name: READTABLE-CASE
candidates.law: Read or set the specified readtable case-conversion mode while preserving mode distinctions.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A table configured :PRESERVE reports :PRESERVE; :UPCASE reports :UPCASE.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Read a different case mode than the table's current mode.

candidates.name: GET-MACRO-CHARACTER
candidates.law: Return the macro-character function and nonterminating flag for an explicit character and readtable.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A character registered with SET-MACRO-CHARACTER is retrieved with its flag.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Forget the nonterminating flag or return a function from a different character.

candidates.name: GET-DISPATCH-MACRO-CHARACTER
candidates.law: Look up the dispatch function assigned to an explicit macro dispatch-char/sub-char pair in a readtable.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A function installed for (#,{) is retrieved for the same pair.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Return that function for an unrelated dispatch sub-character.
